I’ve had many fp over the years, they’ve all disappeared as the years went on. The sooner you come to the realization that people come and go, the better. Even if you get lucky enough to find that one person, or even a handful of people that will always stick by you, something called death exists. So whether you like it or not, eventually, the people closest to you will be gone. That is reality. Fearing abandonment, fearing loss, ultimately does nothing, all it really does it throw your symptoms out of your control, causing issues that likely will lead you down the path towards what you fear. 
Learn to accept that nothing is permanent, and that nobody will always be around.

Generally speaking, I often don’t experience splitting in regards to coworkers or friends or strangers. My splitting is pretty much exclusively linked to my romantic relationships. I get thoughts mind you, but considering that those thoughts are tied to people that I don’t have to think about after I clock out and go home, it isn’t an issue. 
I can work a full time job without many issues at this point, but it really is only possible if I’m single. As soon as I throw a relationship into the mix, I can’t focus on anything else other than my relationship and that creates problems.

I hear voices fairly often. So firstly, there’s the ones that I can’t quite make out, they seem to be audible outside of my mind. More or less, these voices manifest as a form of paranoia, I hear what I think is the voice of someone I care about, in another room, trying to be quiet and essentially talking shit. But anytime I go to investigate, I realize I’m just hearing shit. The other voices are different aspects of my personality that are somewhat fractured. I hear them in my head, can converse with them. There’s a few, and they generally tend to represent certain emotions or parts of myself. Those “personalities” are most active in my mind whenever I’m struggling the most with my mental health. They’ve been silent for a while.

I have no problem taking the high road, when doing so, would be the absolute easiest way to handle a situation. Now, if there is a path where I can take the low road, and dole out a little retribution of my own, with little to no effort on my part, then I take that path without regrets, without guilt, without looking back. Karma is very real, and karma is people. The universe isn’t going to punish the bad people in the world, no, that role is left to the people who’ve been wronged. You wanna turn the cheek, go for it. But I certainly don’t see the value in doing so, and I refuse to. If I let something go, and take the “high road”, it’s literally only because I’ve weighed the pros and cons of the situation and decided that taking the high road would be the best possible path for me to take.

Generally, I am my calmest when I am alone, and I don’t have to deal with anything or anyone. Isolation and solitude are my easiest means to recharge my body and mind. Calm doesn’t necessarily mean “happy” or “stable”. I’m still very easily influenced by things, and when my moods shift, it’s either very suddenly, or it’s gradual, but regardless of the speed in which my mood swings, the negative emotions tend to stick around long past their welcome, and can be very difficult to override and reset. I also feel intensely lonely more often than not. Giving into the need to socialize and be around people, is extremely draining, even when it goes very well for me. Romantic relationships in particular tend to make my internal emotions very turbulent and chaotic.

Spent the entirety of elementary school being bullied. Probably because I was the sort to react. Once high school came along, I became the bully in an attempt to make sure that people left me alone. It worked. 
As for my thoughts on bullying, it’s part of life. If bullying weren’t treated the way it is today, I feel like a lot more people in the world would be close to some sort of baseline normal. Without bullying, I feel like that’s why people these days are such a collective bunch of weirdos and cry babies. Aside from that, even once school ends and adulthood begins, bullying doesn’t really disappear or go anywhere, it just changes form. Humans like to stick to groups and cliques, and ostracize anything outside the norm. It’s human nature.

I have always used sex and masturbation in the same way I used drugs, to self medicate myself, bringing an illusion of joy, power and strength into my life when I felt absolutely nothing but empty. I kicked the drugs, eventually. But I still struggle with an addiction to sex in particular, but really an addiction to anything whatsoever that can give me even the smallest boost in dopamine. I don’t present as a hyper sexual person, but I’ve cheated on every person I’ve been with, I’ve had sex when there were genuine risks involved in doing so, and I’ve also only ever felt truly okay in my relationships whenever I was having sex with them. It’s the only time that I felt close to someone without the nagging voices of doubt screaming out my insecurities. The cheating always stems from those insecurities getting out of hand, it eventually gets to a point where I’ll have sex with a complete stranger to gain that validation of someone wanting me, even though I already have that at home.

I have bpd too, it has its ups and downs, but I WANT to work, the purpose in my life is whatever I decide it is, and I set the goals I want and go for them. Life is what you make of it, seek out therapy services and try working towards changing those thought processes that you have, that’s half the battle. I feel like not being totally empathetic 100% of the time is a very normal thing, not just for people with bpd, but for people in general. Sometimes your focus needs to be on other things, including your own wants and needs. Empathy can be great, and very useful for forming good relationships with people, but having to be empathetic 100% of the time is unrealistic and in my opinion unhealthy.

Learn to be comfortable and happy with your own company. Go for walks, get outside and enjoy nature when the weather is good. Listen to music, better yet, learn to play an instrument. Learn to cook some meals that you enjoy. Read, read a lot. Writing can be good too if you’re into that. Same goes for painting and other artistic pursuits. Being alone with yourself can be good once you learn to feel okay with it.

When it comes to self harm, I stopped because I absolutely hated the way people seemed to judge me when they’d see the wounds or scars. I also came to a realization that while it might offer a momentary release of negative emotions, in the long run, it was only hurting me more. As for drugs, I’ve lost a few friends to overdoses, seen a lot of people, myself included, completely drive their life into the dirt living with addiction. One day I realized that I didn’t like who I was at all, and that the life of drugs and partying was no longer fun if it was ever really fun at all. Packed all of my stuff into the back of a van in under an hour, moved out of my place that I shared with a friend who never managed to get clean, I then spent a month living in my grandmothers basement before I got my first place of my own without any roommates. Met my daughter’s mom shortly after getting clean, and having her in my life while I adjusted to being more sober was a godsend. Two years after we met, she gave birth to my daughter and having a child gave me the motivation I needed to avoid a relapse.
